answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy can work through proof-of-work-gated identity: before an agent may transact, it must publish a stake bonded to a hardware root and pay a recurring compute tax, making each extra puppet identity cost real money. A dishonest swarm that tries to spiral into thousands of accounts must fund every clone, so the marginal cost of the next fake agent never drops to zero. Honest operators treat this rule as an oasis of predictability, while honest newcomers need only one verifiable anchor of history to enter. Verified peers also cross-attest.
